segments.narration: Soviet engineers drilled twelve kilometres down, then stopped. The hole is still there, welded shut, in the Arctic.
Work started on the Kola Peninsula on the twenty-fourth of May, 1970. The target was simply to see how deep a hole could go.
By 1989 the deepest branch reached 12,262 metres. The borehole itself is barely wider than a dinner plate.
Five years earlier they had already lost five kilometres of drill string in the hole. It twisted off and stayed there.
Then heat ended it. In 1992 the rock came in at 180 degrees, far above what the plan allowed. Nothing they had survived it.
